evidence.source: REM-57 gate found a real fail-OPEN adoption path in chooseProjection: `data` was re-redacted but the remote projection's `sections`, `coverage` and the returned `snapshot` were copied VERBATIM, and panel.js feeds those sections straight into PROJECTION.sections and the dashboard cards. So an observer-snapshot.json written by an older or buggy app build could carry a fabricated `reminderHealth` section, reminder fields smuggled inside a known section (reminderBody / occurrenceId / ghToken) and a raw coverage path holding the user's own reminder title into the panel; REM-26 missed it because it only tested the snapshot it built itself. Mirror sections are now always rebuilt locally, only the five raw-derived sections (dailyPhoto, therapyProvenance, profileProgress, notificationTimeline, externalSources) are adopted and are recursively stripped of secret/blob/reminder-namespace keys, unknown section keys are dropped, remote coverage is re-classified with reminder entries masked, and the returned snapshot carries metadata plus sanitized payload only; rich raw-derived values (thoughtCount, responseCount, lifecycle counters) survive and chosen.adoption reports the decision. DECISION REM-ADR-021: the panel reminder surface stays a no-op on separate feature, operator and privacy grounds; the minimum redacted aggregate was rejected; the only exception is REM-53's fixed lifecycle event summary. panel.js was a deliberate no-op because the boundary belongs in the pure adapter every consumer shares
